title: Standard Capital: Dalton Caldwell on rebuilding the Series A with YC's seed-stage playbook
summary: Dalton explains why he launched Standard Capital with Paul Buchheit and Brian Berg: apply the YC seed model (short application, standard terms, founder-set price, fast answer) to the Series A. He argues fundraising is a time sink, valuation is made up, and founder peer groups beat board seats.

principles.text: Fundraising is a distraction from the business; spend as little time on it as possible.
principles.quote: fundraising is a waste of time don't do it like to do it as do it in as short of amount of time as possible.

principles.text: Design the process so the founder's time cost is minimal and the downside is near zero.
principles.quote: the whole point is to have the time cost to a founder to be minimal.

principles.text: Publish standard terms up front so founders know the deal before applying, not after they have said yes.
principles.quote: you'll know exactly what the deal is before you apply instead of it being this opaque thing

principles.text: Early-stage valuation is made-up numbers, so let the founder name their own price.
principles.quote: There's no equation. Everyone just makes up numbers.

principles.text: Replace board seats with a curated founder peer group; the best advice comes from other operators.
principles.quote: the best advice you're going to get from as a founder is from other founders and from peers that you respect.

principles.text: Help each founder find the one idea where they have the most unfair advantages.
principles.quote: I believe that every person has like a perfect idea for them
